title: The great schism and the Paladins
summary: How the Chorus split between Rome and Constantinople.

claims.text: Rapid growth set Western Singers seeking supremacy for Rome against Eastern Singers who wanted equal standing.
The Cabal of Pure Thought urged that the Byzantines be brought in by force, but the Pontifex and the Curia refused and allowed some difference.
In the 800s militant Singers moved from Rome to Aachen and became the Palatine Knights, or Paladins, sworn to guard humanity from darkness.

title: The fall of the Temple, 1307
summary: The suppression of the Templars as the Chorus remembers it.

claims.text: King Philip the Fair had the French Templars seized in 1307 on heresy charges, with papal leave, and is widely thought to have wanted their wealth.
Over seven years knights were tortured and tried; some burned, while most recanted and entered other Orders.
Grand Master Jacques de Molay is said to have planned a sacrifice to shield the Order while the rest gathered much of its fortune and slipped from public life.

title: The Templar Knights in the Chorus today
summary: A small remnant of holy warriors.

claims.text: Fewer than 30 fully knighted members are known, and some of them do not use Sphere magic.
The survivors argue over pressing on or pulling back to train recruits; those with prophetic gifts hint that either choice may not matter.
The Knights favour Forces and lean on sorcerer consors skilled in Alchemy and Enchantment for their gear.

title: The Order of St. Michael
summary: A fast-growing Chorus order of local protectors.

claims.text: Founded in the 1950s among early liberation theologians of Central America, it sets out to bring justice and mercy to those denied both.
Once tiny, it grew sharply after the Reckoning thanks to its near-vigilante focus on local action.
It takes few apprentices, welcomes Choristers who want to guard their own communities, and targets big corporations, organised crime and corrupt officials.

title: Monists
summary: The Chorus thinkers who preach that all faiths are one.

claims.text: Monists hold that every faith, person and creation is part of the One, and that differences come only from human limits.
It is not a formal faction, yet most seasoned Choristers share some Monist belief.
Monists are the Singers most likely to work with other Traditions, so outsiders often judge the Chorus by them.

title: Alexandrians
summary: Choristers who seek to reconcile faith and technology.

claims.text: Alexandrians argue that anything created has a purpose from the One and that reason is as valid a tool as faith.
They prune outdated theology and cope with the modern age better than almost any other Chorus group.

title: Rastafarians, Sikhs and Sufis in the Chorus

claims.text: Rastafarian Singers name the One as Jah and some study the Sphere of Time.
Sikhs rarely join the Chorus since some of their leaders forbid miracle-working; most Sikh Singers focus on Prime.
Tales link Awakened Sikhs to the near-forgotten Ahl-i-Batin, though no Sikh Singer has confirmed them.
More Awakened Sufis now join Chorus Chantries, trading old insight for shelter, and are rumoured to guard hidden Batini treasures.

title: The Merovingians and Prester John
summary: Legends of holy bloodlines and a Christian emperor of Asia.

claims.text: A legend claims a secret Brotherhood of Zion created the Templars and built churches on ley lines by sacred geometry, perhaps even helping found the Technocracy.
Some Choristers once claimed Merovingian blood and Sang by right of long hair, chalice and crown; they vanished when the Templars appeared.
Medieval clergy, mundane and Singer alike, told of Prester John, a Christian emperor of Asia and a mage whose lands held the Garden of Eden.
